title: What must this landing do?
question: Surface is `/` (logged-out). Logged-in people already skip this for the dashboard. Functional Clarity stays. Confirm the job, success, and what a builder must not touch. Steer if the waitlist, playground, or logo-first hero is on the table.

options.label: Prove the handshake, then join
options.thesis: In the first viewport they know this is a digital handshake, not a feed. The only hero action is Join the Waitlist. Playground below fold is the demo, not a screenshot farm.
options.body: Keep: logo mark, tagline, one CTA + About, login in the navbar, no Insights on `/`, no ads/feed claims, waitlist (app not publicly launched), playground maps as they are (Carto, Seattle clamp, no Worker tiles). Untouched: PRODUCT.md facts, DESIGN.md tokens, auth callbacks. Success: they can say “phones verify we were in the same room” and they submit the waitlist. Scope: whole landing composition may be reshaped inside Functional Clarity; this is a production-ready page brief, not a new brand.

options.label: First viewport only
options.thesis: Shape just the fold: mark, line, waitlist. Below-fold Why / How / Playground / Mission / Enterprise / close stay as-is.
options.body: Success is still waitlist, but the brief will not reopen playground or enterprise placement. Smaller structural invention.
options.case: Local extension of an established surface — no composition tournament later.

options.label: Get the app, not the waitlist
options.thesis: The landing’s job is store download / open-in-app, waitlist is secondary or gone.
options.body: Only pick this if launch state has changed. PRODUCT.md still lists waitlist until NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_LAUNCHED. Use the note to name iOS/Android store facts we must not invent.
options.case: Conflicts with current launch posture unless you override it.

options.label: Different job
options.thesis: The landing must make someone believe or do a different thing than waitlist-after-handshake.
options.body: Use the note: who arrives, what they must do, what would feel wrong even if it looked polished.
options.case: For a third audience, event-first landing, or operator-first `/`.
